description: Verify that DUT-emitted UDP datagrams with even payload size carry no trailing padding bytes (RFC 768 'Fields')
approach:
[Objective]
UDP itself never adds padding. With an even-length payload there is no checksum-related zero-pad either. The wire frame must end exactly at (UDP header + payload); any trailing bytes mean DUT is leaking buffer contents or aligning at the wrong layer.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpTriggerSendUdp request with an even-length payload

2. Observation:
   • DUT → Tester: UDP datagram
     - IP Total Length corresponds exactly to (IP header + UDP header + payload), no extra octets   ← key check

[Pass condition]
DUT-emitted UDP frame has no trailing padding past the declared payload.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_padding_or_length — DUT emitted UDP with trailing bytes beyond the payload (or wrong Length field)
• Fail_timeout — DUT did not emit any UDP within the listen window

verdicts.Pass: DUT-emitted even-payload UDP has no trailing padding — normal
verdicts.Fail_padding_or_length: DUT emitted UDP with trailing padding on even payload
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT-originated UDP within the listen window
